content_of_post_to_comment: It’s interesting that people often seem to think there’s a pure, friendly core to every religion that is secularly-liberally tolerable, and everything else about a religion is an outside corruption of this pure spirit. Sometimes religions are simply not palatable to people outside them and there’s no scapegoat.
comment: A useful distinction might be between internal diversity and external compatibility: a tradition can contain plural interpretations while still having core commitments that conflict with liberal assumptions.
